NYC can feel SO overwhelming when you’re planning your first trip with kids.

So if it were my kids’ first time, I’d keep it simple and focus on the iconic NYC experiences. 🗽🏙️

DAY 1 ✨ Times Square
🍕 NYC pizza 🎭 Broadway show

DAY 2 🗽 Statue of Liberty 💰 9/11 Memorial + Museum 🥟 Chinatown 🌉 Brooklyn Bridge at sunset

DAY 3
🥯 NYC bagel 🏙️ SUMMIT One Vanderbilt
🌳 Central Park 🏙️ Fifth Avenue

A few tips I’d keep in mind:

✨ Stay somewhere central if you can. Midtown makes it easy to walk to a ton of attractions and gives you convenient subway access for everything else.

✨ Group attractions by neighborhood. Do your Statue of Liberty, 9/11 Memorial, Chinatown and Brooklyn Bridge day together instead of wasting time going back and forth across Manhattan.

✨ See a Broadway show if your budget allows. This has been one of the biggest highlights of our NYC trips!

✨ I used the Wanderlog app to keep all of our plans organized and to map everything out by location. 

✨ And bring comfortable shoes. On day 2 we walked over 25K steps

media.transcript: If I were taking my kids to New York City for the first time, here's exactly what I would do. I'd stay somewhere in Midtown so we could walk almost everywhere. On day one, I'd start with Times Square, grab lunch at Joe's Pizza, and finish the day with a Broadway show. On day two, I would take the subway to Lower Manhattan to see the Statue of Liberty, visit the 9-11 Memorial and Museum, grab food in Chinatown, and walk the Brooklyn Bridge. And finally, on day three, I'd start with a New York bagel, do one big observation deck. We loved Summit 1 Vanderbilt with kids. Then walk down Fifth Avenue and through Central Park. You don't have to see it all on your first trip, just pick a few iconic experiences, walk as much as you can, and leave room to just experience the city.

Originally from Nashville, Tennessee, we got married 2013 and were super “normal.” I was a teacher and Nate started a small printing business from the spare bedroom of our apartment.

Our goal was to see as many places as possible before we ran out of money and went back home to “normal life.” We started this channel to share our experiences with friends and family, but quickly fell in love with living on the road and found a new passion for capturing our travels through video. So we did everything we could to keep going.

4 years later, we achieved our new goal of visiting 100 countries and all 7 continents. We had no plans to slow down, until 2020 forced us to ;) Which is when we bought a converted van to start exploring our own country for the first time!

After ~2 years of van life, we are back to full time international traveling! And now we are in our 11TH YEAR of finding the best adventures the world has to offer :) 

We are incredibly grateful to be able to continue doing something we love every day. 😊🎥🌎 Thank you to everyone who has been a part of our journey!

results.caption: Which one do you prefer? China can look completely different during the day versus the night, and both are stunning in its own way! During our recent trip to China, we explored ancient towns and mountains during the day, and experience the vibrant city life at night. If you are thinking about a trip to China, save this guide and follow for more China travel inspo!  🌃 CHONGQING 🟢 Hongyadong 洪崖洞 is best visited around sunset so you can see it before and after the lights turn on.  🟢 Liziba Station 李子坝站 is where Chongqing’s Line 2 monorail appears to travel directly through a building.  🟢 Luohan Temple 罗汉寺 is a peaceful Buddhist temple surrounded by Chongqing’s skyscrapers. 🐼 CHENGDU 🟢 Visit the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding early in the morning when pandas tend to be more active. 🟢 Head to Chunxi Road and Taikoo Li after dark for shopping, food and the giant 3D panda screen. 🟢 Tower of Life is especially impressive after dark when the structure is illuminated. ⛰️ ZHANGJIAJIE 🟢 Allow at least 2 - 3 days for Zhangjiajie National Forest Park. Highlights include Yuanjiajie, Tianzi Mountain and the Bailong Elevator. 🟢 Stay near Wulingyuan for easier access to the national park. 🟢 Add Tianmen Mountain if you have another day. It is a separate attraction closer to Zhangjiajie city. 🏮 FURONG TOWN 🟢 This ancient town is built directly around a waterfall and is best experienced after dark when the buildings illuminate. 💧 DUJIANGYAN 🟢 Visit the Dujiangyan Irrigation System, an engineering project dating back more than 2,000 years that still helps control and distribute water today. 🟢 After dark, head into Dujiangyan city to see the famous glowing blue water known online as the Blue Tears. 🌆 GUANGZHOU 🟢 Head to the Canton Tower and the Zhujiang New Town waterfront around sunset. Stay after dark to see the tower and Guangzhou’s modern skyline illuminated along the Pearl River. 🟢 Explore Yongqing Fang 永庆坊 and the surrounding Xiguan area for historic Cantonese architecture alongside restored shops, cafés and restaurants. 🟢 Make time for Dim Sum while you’re here! Minden nap 15 és 20 ezer lépés között fogok menni. Heti háromszor edzek, nálam ez most három darab futást jelent, majd idővel meglátjuk, hogy lesz-e más is. Minden nap valamilyen tanulás vagy olvasás. Rend és tisztaság, minden nap 10-15 perc arra, hogy rendet rakjak. Kevesebb screen time, hogyha minden más teljesítek, akkor ez már amúgy adja magát. Head to the App Store and download MapQuest. Open it and click Get Started, then choose your icon. I chose a blue dot. Hit Ask App Not to Track, and then click the Layers button. From here you see the Surveillance Layers, so turn that on. And voila, all the flock cameras around you. If you zoom too far out, they disappear, so zoom in closer. You can click on them to see the angle of their field of view, and you can also see what type of camera they are, and their exact GPS coordinates. media.transcript: If you're planning to come to Korea and you're looking for an easy way to travel and do fun things, then this is the video for you. Traveling in Korea can be quite stressful, especially when there's too many things to do. That's why I decided to show you a great way to travel in Korea, and it's called the Trip Builder app. All you have to do is find places on Instagram that you want to visit and save them directly onto the app, like eating Dakarvi, visiting the popular Songsoo, and even the famous library at Koek. The app will find all the locations for you, and you can even ask the AI travel assistant to create you an entire itinerary based off the places you chose. And my favorite part is that you can access the K-Ride app directly through Trip Builder and take a taxi to one of the places that you save. This is such an easy, stress-free way to travel around Korea, and I highly recommend it to those who want to travel around but don't know how to start. If you're interested to try them out, they even have an event going on where you can save three places on Trip Builder and use the K-Ride ones to receive a 5,000 won Olive Young or Starbucks gift card.
